sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the commercial centre of Bridgeton on the east bank of the Cohansey River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. East Commerce Street runs diagonally up the sheet from the river and the iron bridge at the left edge, crossing Cohansey, North and South Laurel and North and South Pearl Streets, and the blocks on either side are solid rows of two and three storey brick stores. Named buildings include the Bridgetonian Hotel, a telephone exchange, banks, a department store, the Stanley Theatre and the Stanley Building at Pearl Street, the Criterion Theatre, the Hotel Belvidere, the Eagles Club house, the Loom Club house, the Moose Home, the Laurel Hotel, the Salvation Army building, the Cumberland County Mutual Fire Insurance Co. and the Cumberland Trust Co. There are several garages and auto sales and service buildings, and a printing works and ice and cold storage plant near the river. In the upper left the Atlantic City Electric Co. Bridgeton substation and power house stand on the bank above the river, with boilers, transformers, a furniture warehouse and a printing works below them. Warren Street branches east from South Laurel Street, and Jefferson Street runs across the bottom of the sheet, with Lemon Street and South Pearl Street at the lower right corner. Church Lane forms the top edge of the central block row. Six, twelve and sixteen inch water mains are marked in the streets. The Cohansey River fills the left side, with a compass rose on the water. Neighbouring sheets 8, 9, 3, 4, 21 and 20 are named in the margins.
notes: Printed Jefferson is East Broad Street in OpenStreetMap; the junction of North Pearl, South Pearl and East Broad Street is at the lower right.
Printed Cohansey (a street) is Cohansey Street in OpenStreetMap; printed East and West Commerce are Commerce Street East and West Commerce Street.
Detector settings: ink_below_paper 45. Control: five detected junctions on East Commerce, Laurel, Warren and Cohansey, plus one hand-picked fork at Pearl and Jefferson (East Broad Street).
map, 50 ft: downtown centre, E. Commerce / Laurel / Pearl; Cohansey River at left; E. Broad / S. Laurel left out (modern S. Laurel 9-25 m west of the drawn line)

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the eastern edge of Bridgeton's business district and the residential streets beyond it, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north arrow and compass at the top. East Commerce Street crosses the upper part of the sheet diagonally from South Pearl Street at the left to Walnut Street and Pine Street at the top right corner. South Pearl Street forms the left edge, and Lemon Street, drawn with Jefferson Street at the lower left, crosses the bottom. The civic buildings stand along the north side of the block between Pearl and Orange Streets: City Hall, the Bridgeton Free Library, the American Legion Club house, a jail and fire department building, and the First Baptist Church. The Cumberland Hotel, a large fireproof building, occupies the corner at Pearl Street. Warren Street, Elizabeth Street and Orange Street cross the middle of the sheet. The lower left blocks hold garages, used auto sales and repairing, a sausage factory, a warehouse, lodge rooms, a wholesale grocery, scrap iron storage and the Mary S. Fithian Memorial Chapel. J. P. Shaw and Co. have a paint factory on Orange Street. St. Andrews Episcopal Church and its chapel stand in the upper right with a few scattered dwellings. The south east part of the sheet is lightly built with small frame dwellings and stores along Orange Street and East Lemon Street, and the large block between Bank Street and the edge of the drawing is nearly empty. The right side of the sheet is blank, drawn on sheets 14 and 7, and the edges adjoin sheets 9, 2 and 4.
notes: Printed Jefferson Street (west of the Pearl Street fork) and Lemon (east of it) are East Broad Street in OpenStreetMap.
Elizabeth Street and East Lemon Street are not in the OpenStreetMap extract under these names and were not used for control.
East Commerce Street at Walnut Street was not detected; the modern Walnut Street junction projects about 5 m east of the drawn one, so it was left out.
The detected fork of North Pearl, South Pearl and East Broad Street lies about 10 m from where the drawn pipes meet; parcel centre and drawn fork disagree, so confidence there is low.
map, 50 ft: E. Commerce east of Pearl, Orange, Bank, Warren; Walnut / E. Commerce not used

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the south end of Bridgeton's business district and the industrial waterfront on the east bank of the Cohansey River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a compass rose at the left. South Laurel Street runs diagonally down the middle of the sheet from Jefferson Street at the top to Glass Street, and South Pearl Street runs parallel to it on the east, with Mulberry Street crossing between them. Jefferson Street and Lemon form the top edge. The upper part is a mixed district of stores, garages, a gymnasium, a printing works, farm implement and hay storage, a wagon repair shop, a planing mill, the Crystal Laundry, a bakery, an abattoir and cold packing house, and rows of dwellings and attached shops. The Passenger Station and a freight house stand beside the railroad, whose tracks sweep in a wide curve down the right side of the sheet and cross Pearl Street and Glass Street. At the left are the lumber yards of Smith and Richards, with lumber sheds and piles and a coal yard, a garage and machine shop, and warehouses on the river bank. A city sewage pump house and filter tank stand beside Glass Street. The lower part of the sheet is occupied by the extensive canning factory of P. J. Ritter Co., with its warehouses, can house and other numbered buildings, sprinklered and fitted with water spray equipment, and a note on the watchman, fire protection and power equipment. The Cohansey River fills the lower left, with a basin and oil tanks at the bottom edge. Neighbouring sheets 2, 3, 5, 20, 21 and 24 are named in the margins.
notes: Printed Jefferson and Lemon at the top are East Broad Street in OpenStreetMap.
Mulberry is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.

Control is weak: the junction of North Pearl, South Pearl and East Broad Street was detected, and the junctions of South Laurel Street with East Broad Street and with Glass Street are hand-picked. The modern South Laurel Street lies several metres west of the drawn one, and the modern Glass Street and South Pearl Street junction projects about 20 m from where the detector measured it, so the placement is low confidence.
map, 50 ft: S. Laurel / S. Pearl / Glass, cannery, railroad; detector finds almost nothing; placed from hand picks (low confidence)

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the south side of Bridgeton between Grove Street and South Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a compass rose in the upper left. South Pearl Street runs across the top, and Grove Street and South Avenue run down the sheet, the second bending diagonally at the top where it meets South Pearl Street and Willow Street. Eagle Street crosses from Grove Street to South Avenue, and Henry Street forms the bottom edge. The district between the two streets is residential, with rows of small detached frame dwellings on narrow lots, a Pentecostal Mission and, on the east side of South Avenue, the John Wesley M. E. Church and a garage marked as not in operation. Henry R. Dix and Sons Co., a uniform factory, stands at the upper right beside Willow Street. West of Grove Street the sheet is industrial: the Marshall Lime and Cement Co. with abandoned lime kilns and storage, a cement block works, a cement and lime warehouse, and, at the lower left, canning factories belonging to E. Pritchard and to H. Hettinger Bros, formerly the Garrett Bergen Co., with warehouses, a boiler house, canning shop, pulp shed and numbered buildings, each with a note on night watchman, power, lights and hose. A railroad curves through the sheet from the lower left to the upper right, where several tracks of the W. J. and S. R. R. and Pine Street converge. Mill Creek winds down the left side towards the Cohansey River at the bottom corner, and a drawing of a burned building, labelled as ruins of fire, stands at the left. Sheets 4, 6, 7, 17, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32 and 38 are named in the margins.
notes: Control is detected junctions of Eagle Street and Henry Street with Grove Street and South Avenue and of Willow Street with South Avenue. The junction of South Avenue with South Pearl Street was not used: the modern node projects about 14 m from the drawn pipe junction.
Printed South Av. is South Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Pine in the upper right is Pine Street or South Pine Street there (not used for control).
map, 50 ft: S. Pearl, Grove, Eagle, South Av, Willow, Henry; canning works, Mill Creek

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the south-western edge of Bridgeton along the east bank of the Cohansey River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a compass rose at the left. Henry Street runs across the top of the sheet, Grove Street comes in from sheet 5 at the top and ends in open ground, and South Avenue runs the full height of the sheet on the right, with River Street crossing from it towards the river in the lower middle. A private lane forms the bottom edge of the middle block. The built-up area is a strip of detached frame dwellings with small outbuildings along South Avenue and on the blocks west of it, with the 4th M. E. Church, a parsonage and the Second M. P. Church on the avenue and The South Av. Public School at the lower right. At the top left Hettinger Engine Co., manufacturers of gasoline engines, occupy a machine shop and storage buildings, with a boat shop, a repair shop and storage sheds on the river bank, and a pier at the left edge. Along the river below them the bank is lined with scattered small dwellings and sheds reached by Alton Place, a lane running parallel to the shore. Most of the left half of the sheet is open land and water: the Cohansey River winds down the left edge with a sharply curving shoreline, and the large blocks between the lanes and the river are blank. Water mains of four and six inches are marked in the streets. Sheets 5, 32, 38 and 39 adjoin on the margins, with lot and block numbers 102, 103 and 220 printed in the blocks.
notes: Printed South Av. is South Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Alton Place and Private Lane are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Modern Grove Street continues south to River Street, but Grove Street is not drawn south of the open lots; the junction the detector found there was excluded.
Control is three junctions on Henry Street and River Street with South Avenue and Grove Street, so the fit is exact through three points: low confidence.
map, 50 ft: Henry, Grove, South Av, River; Cohansey River bank; three-point fit

sheet-7-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 7, covering the east side of Bridgeton where East Commerce Street leaves the built-up centre. The map is bounded at the top by East Commerce Street and runs down the page along Pine Street, which carries two rows of closely spaced dwellings, mostly two or two and a half storeys, with small outbuildings at the rear of each lot. Pine Street meets East Commerce at the top left and, at the lower left, meets Mill, which runs north-east from that corner, turns north along the lots west of Mill Place and then bends east across the lower part of the page. Mill Place is a narrow way running north from Mill beside a block of auto wrecking yards. The upper right is occupied by the M. E. Cemetery, an unbuilt tract of block 209 with the 1st M. E. Church, a pink brick building marked as heated by furnace and lit by electricity, standing on East Commerce Street at its north-west corner. A lane runs south-east from East Commerce along the east edge of the cemetery. East of Mill Place the land is largely open, with scattered dwellings and one larger building near the right edge. Six inch water pipes lie in Pine Street, Mill and East Commerce Street. The north arrow is drawn on the cemetery and the sheet is at 50 feet to an inch. Heavy lines cut out the inset at the lower right and a small piece at the lower left, which are separate parts. Adjoining sheets named in the margins are 3 to the west, 14 and 5 to the south-west and 38 and 11 to the south.
notes: The word Arbitrary is printed along Mill Place; the printed name of the lane east of the cemetery is Lane alone.
Only two street junctions (East Commerce / Pine and Mill / Pine) are available on this part, both on Pine Street; it is a two-point helmert fit and low confidence.
Modern OpenStreetMap names: East Commerce is East Commerce Street, Pine is Pine Street, Mill is Mill Street; Mill Place and Lane are not in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-7-2.description: Part 2 is the inset in the lower right of sheet 7, enclosed by a heavy line and drawn with its own north arrow pointing straight up. It shows East Commerce, here running across the upper part of the inset from west to east, and the blocks on its south side numbered 274 to 328, which are filled with detached frame dwellings and a small number of outbuildings, one of them a brick-coloured dwelling marked Br. 1st, and a blue-coloured building in the rear lots. East Avenue is drawn at the right edge, lettered N. East Av. north of East Commerce and S. East Av. to the south, with six and eight inch water pipes along it and a sixteen inch pipe in East Commerce. A telephone hole marks the East Commerce and East Avenue corner. A broad curved private way inside block 209 serves a group of rear buildings, and the southern part of the inset carries more dwellings fronting Mill, which runs across the bottom of the inset and meets South East Avenue at the lower right. The inset is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The ground north of the heavy line belongs to the main part of the sheet, and the areas marked 38 and 11 beyond the inset are drawn on those sheets.
notes: Only the East Commerce / East Avenue junction was detected; the part is anchored on it with the atlas scale and a rotation from its measured lines, and is low confidence.
The drawn spacing between the East Commerce and Mill junctions on East Avenue is about 5 percent shorter than the modern one.
Modern OpenStreetMap names: North East Avenue and South East Avenue are East Avenue and South East Avenue.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the area north of Bridgeton's main business street, between the Cohansey River and North Pearl Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a compass rose at the left. Washington Street crosses the sheet from left to right about two thirds of the way down. Cohansey Street runs down the left of the middle, North Laurel Street down the centre and North Pearl Street along the right edge, and Church Lane forms the bottom edge in front of the Bell Telephone Co. building, the First Presbyterian Church and its Sunday school. North of Washington Street the blocks are mainly detached dwellings on narrow lots, with a synagogue, a plumber, auto painting and upholstering and auto washing shops. Along the river at the upper left the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs beside a coal trestle, with its passenger station and freight depot, and the Swift and Co. wholesale meat house and a feed warehouse beside it. Abbott's Alderney Dairies Inc., a milk station and ice cream factory with freezing tanks, cold storage and a packing house, occupies the block at the left above a garage, a bottling works and the Armory of Co. K, 3rd Regiment, N. G. N. J. Below Washington Street at the left are the Morvay and Sons Inc. ladies underwear factory, the Cumberland Traction Co. car barn and a large lumber yard, and at the centre the Geo. Maier and Bro. lumber yard, planing mill and builders supplies, an auto service station and garages. South of Washington Street on the right stand a feed mill, furniture and candy manufacturers, a hall and stores. A scrap iron yard lies on the river bank. The Cohansey River runs down the left side. Adjoining sheets 14, 12, 9, 2, 20 and 3 are named in the margins.
notes: Printed N. Laurel and N. Pearl are North Laurel Street and North Pearl Street in OpenStreetMap; Cohansey is Cohansey Street.

The narrow street at the lower left of the dairy block, with a 14 inch water main, matches Sharp Street in OpenStreetMap, a service road, which is why the config sets service_roads. It is not lettered on the sheet.
Most control lies along Washington Street, so the rotation rests mainly on that one line; Cohansey Street and Sharp Street gives the second direction and agrees with it.
